name: b2f-block-protocol
summary: Fenced-code-block file protocol. A block whose info string carries file= is a write proposal; the runtime publishes all blocks of one assistant message as a single Git commit before any tool call in that message executes.
rationale: This is deliberately not a DSH tool seam. Proposals must be observable in the assistant message itself and must commit atomically as a group, which a per-call tool interface cannot express.

file.description: Repository-relative target path. Absolute paths, drive letters, and `.`/`..` segments are rejected.

mode.description: edit and diff are partial-edit dialects; exactly one of them is accepted per deployment, selected by the editFormat configuration.

newline.description: Rejected on edit and diff blocks, which preserve the file's existing line endings.

replace.body: One or more `<<<<<<< SEARCH` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> REPLACE` sections.
rules: Each SEARCH must match the observed content exactly once.
Matched spans must be pairwise disjoint.
An empty REPLACE deletes the matched span.

git_diff.body: Hunk-only unified diff. File headers (diff --git, index, ---, +++) are tolerated but not required.
rules: Stated hunk line counts are ignored and recomputed from the body.
The @@ start line is a hint; the anchor is located by context search, nearest match winning, within maxEditDrift lines.

resolution.description: Every proposal, full-content or partial, is resolved against the blob the model observed rather than the worktree, which is a managed projection. Partial edits resolve in-process and never route through `git apply`, so no clean/smudge filter or apply configuration can alter the proposed bytes.

transaction.publication: single commit on the canonical ref via compare-and-swap
transaction.atomicity: If any block is stale, fails a precondition, would overwrite local drift, or has an unresolvable edit anchor, nothing is committed.

feedback.echoNote: Informational content echoes are labelled path=, never file=, so a verbatim copy-back by the model is inert and writes nothing.
